28                                   AURORA

brought itself forward. Indeed, arsenic certainly cannot be fixed unless the operating artist has an equal knowledge of its tingeing spirit, in which matter all the philosophers have slumbered, attempting in vain to produce something from it. Therefore, whoever is ignorant of this spirit should have no hope of fixing it, nor of bestowing upon it the virtue by which it might acquire the perfection of transmutation. For this reason, I make it known to all that the whitening about which mention has been made was derived from a false foundation, and by that means copper is falsely whitened, not transmuted. Sophists, having disguised and painted Venus <note>the metal copper</note> in this manner, mixed it with double its own amount of lunar <note>silver</note> metal and sold it to goldsmiths and coiners. Finally, they transformed themselves into false coiners, not only those who sold it, but even those who bought it. Some of the sophists, in place of white, took red arsenic, and this also went into a false art. For in whatever way it is prepared, it exhibits nothing except whiteness. Some proceeded further to common sulfur, which they cooked so yellow with vinegar, lye, or very sharp urine, day and night, until it emerged white. Afterward, they elevated it from common salt and eggshells through sublimation and cooked it, and sublimed it, and this many times; nevertheless, it always remained combustible, even though it was white. Yet, [it was] for this [reason] to fix crude mercury <column-break/>

<summary>This page warns practitioners against using common arsenic, sulfur, and false techniques to "whiten" metals, labeling such methods as the work of deceptive "sophists" who produce unstable results.</summary>
